comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C5, C39, C41-C48. Both evaluations find the biochemical characterization of TrGSDME cleavage by CASP3/7 to be convincing and well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes multiple lines of evidence; peer reviewers describe the data as 'convincing' with 'diverse biochemical assays.'

Perfect agreement on claims C49-C57. Both evaluations support the cellular pyroptosis data showing TrGSDME-NT is pyroptotic and requires caspase cleavage. OpenEval highlights convergent evidence from multiple assays; peer reviewers acknowledge the data without methodological concerns.

Perfect agreement on claims C4, C40, C58-C59. Both evaluations strongly support the differential cleavage observation as a central finding. OpenEval notes substrate discrimination beyond motif recognition; peer reviewers describe this as an 'important contribution' with 'convincing biochemical and mutational data.'

Strong agreement on claims C60-C64 regarding CT domain control of CASP7 recognition. OpenEval notes uncertainty about structural features due to modeling rather than experimental structures; peer reviewers explicitly praise the domain swapping approach as a strength. Peer result also includes C6-C7 not in OpenEval result.

Perfect agreement on claims C65-C71. Both evaluations strongly support the p10 domain swapping experiments showing p10 mediates substrate specificity. OpenEval emphasizes the importance of C67 (tetrapeptide activity retention); peer reviewers commend the chimeric approach as part of rigorous methodology.

Strong agreement on claims C72-C77, C81-C85 regarding S234 mutagenesis. Both evaluations praise the systematic approach. OpenEval emphasizes reciprocal mutation effects and cellular validation; peer reviewers specifically highlight the 'unbiased mutagenesis screen' as a major strength. Peer result also includes C8, C79-C80.

Partial overlap on claims C79-C80. OpenEval groups these with C78 as evidence against exosite involvement, noting the conclusion is somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers include C79-C80 with the broader mutagenesis findings (R6) and accept them as part of the comprehensive analysis without specific concerns.

Perfect agreement on claims C86-C90. Both evaluations support the CASP3 N208 findings extending the S234 discovery. OpenEval notes the effect is 'much weaker' rather than abolished; peer reviewers treat this as part of comprehensive mutational analysis supporting the broader conclusion about residue importance.

Perfect agreement on claims C9-C11, C91-C94, C123-C124. Both evaluations support the evolutionary sequence analysis showing CASP7 divergence in primates. OpenEval notes functional significance requires experimental validation; peer reviewers accept the bioinformatics component as supporting main conclusions about molecular divergence.

Strong agreement on claims C12, C95-C98 regarding cross-species cleavage patterns. Both evaluations support evidence for independent evolution. OpenEval emphasizes the striking observation about mouse CASP7/GSDME; peer reviewers accept the data but note physiological implications remain unclear. Peer result excludes C99-C100.

Partial overlap on claims C99-C100. OpenEval groups these with C12, C95-C98 as evidence for independent evolution; peer reviewers group C99-C100 with C129-C130 as evolutionary interpretation, accepting it as valid inference about diversification and specialization of gasdermins.

Strong agreement on claims C125-C127, C130-C131. Both evaluations rate these as UNCERTAIN, recognizing them as speculative interpretations about evolutionary and physiological significance lacking direct experimental support. OpenEval notes no functional data for proposed consequences; peer reviewers explicitly state 'lacks physiological relevance' and future studies are needed.

Partial overlap on claim C129. OpenEval groups C128-C129 as SUPPORTED evolutionary interpretation connecting to prior literature; peer reviewers include C129 with C99-C100, C130 as SUPPORTED evolutionary conclusions about diversification and specialization, treating them as valid inferences from the data.

Partial overlap on claim C41. OpenEval includes C41 in R1 as SUPPORTED phylogenetic classification evidence; peer reviewers raise UNCERTAIN concern about C41 specifically, requesting clarification about which GSDME paralog (GSDMEa vs GSDMEb) was studied and discussion of differential function in fish.

Strong agreement on claims C103-C112 regarding teleost GSDME literature. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED context from prior work, noting interpretation about functional diversification is speculative; peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, requesting more thorough integration of teleost GSDME literature and clearer discussion of functional implications.

OpenEval evaluates claims C114-C117 as SUPPORTED regarding distinct engagement modes for GSDME versus other substrates, noting the conclusion is somewhat inferential. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific mechanistic claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims C118-C122 as SUPPORTED regarding the systematic dissection showing p10 swapping and specific residue identification. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these methodological claims about negative and positive results.

OpenEval evaluates claims C1-C3, C13-C37, C44 as SUPPORTED established knowledge from literature providing necessary context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these background claims are not typically evaluated separately by peer reviewers.
